steps.path: Settings → Remote Access, and a conversation on your phone or browser
steps.headline: This is what done means for remote access: setup, the devices list, and reconnecting.

rows.statement: Remote access setup guides you through each step, explains every change before it happens, and checks the connection at the end.
rows.threshold: a dev instance is walked through setup end to end

rows.statement: A message typed while the connection is down waits as a draft until you press Send yourself; nothing runs again on its own.
rows.threshold: the draft survives a disconnect in a dev instance and sends only when pressed

rows.statement: Your phone stays on the conversation you had open; changing conversations on the desktop does not move it.
rows.threshold: the phone keeps its conversation across a desktop switch and a reconnect, in a dev instance

rows.statement: Enabled, Password, Keep awake and Add Device stay exactly where they are in the Remote Access panel.
The panel opens saying remote access is not set up yet, with one button forward, instead of warning about your phone.
One yellow box asks your permission before this computer's name goes into a public certificate record.
Devices are listed by name, and removing one really removes its access — it has to pair again.
The button that removes a device's access reads Unpair, and confirming it says the device must pair again.
Skip password on Tailscale is gone; a device needs the password even on your own private network.
